surtitre: ECC system conversion to S/4HANA · SAP Activate
titre: A brownfield migration to S/4HANA, from A to Z
intro: The six SAP Activate phases on a timeline. Click a bar, a quality gate or the go-live to open the details.

exemple.description: Ternova (fictional), parts distributor, ECC since 2009 converted to S/4HANA

chronologieAria: Brownfield conversion timeline: SAP Activate phases, steps and quality gates from M-12 to M+2
enContinu: governance, ECC freeze, risks, downtime duration
causesTitre: The 5 most common causes of failure
note: Typical approach and indicative durations for a medium scope, to be adapted to each program. Discover takes place before the project starts. The example figures are fictional.

s1.s: Convert the existing system rather than start from scratch
s1.obj: Decide to convert the existing ECC system to S/4HANA, and in which deployment model.
act: Assessment of the current landscape: processes, custom code, volumes
Comparison of greenfield, brownfield and bluefield
First SAP Readiness Check and recommendations report
Budget and high-level schedule, taking the end of ECC maintenance into account
pre: Access to the production ECC system for analysis
Vision of the constraints: deadline, budget, business capacity
s1.ex: Ternova has run on ECC since 2009. Its processes work well and the business does not want to redesign everything. End of maintenance is approaching: the migration has to be quick. Choice: brownfield, conversion to S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition via RISE. Budget of €4M, go-live targeted for a long weekend in May.
ai: Analysis of actual transaction and custom code usage
Comparative summary of the three approaches
r: Brownfield chosen 'because it is simpler': the bad processes are kept too
List from the start what you want to improve after the conversion
End-of-maintenance date dictates everything: unrealistic schedule
Plan backwards from the date, with a margin

s2.obj: Get the project up and running, with a team suited to a conversion.
act: Conversion team: technical lead, Basis, developers
Contracts with the integrator and the hosting provider
s2.ex: The team is more technical than in a greenfield: a conversion lead, developers for the custom code, a Basis team. The business is less involved, but key users remain essential for testing.
r: Project seen as 'purely technical': the business disengages
Key users named and reserved for testing from the launch
Unclear roles between integrator, hosting provider and SAP
RACI signed by all three

s3.obj: Measure precisely what the conversion imposes: simplification items, code, add-ons, volumes.
act: Running the Readiness Check on production
Inventory of custom code and its usage
pre: SAP Notes and collectors installed on ECC
Functional and technical experts to read the report
s3.ex: The report lists 45 relevant simplification items. The heaviest: Business Partner, the Universal Journal and the end of LE-WM. 1,500 custom objects, 40% never executed in two years. A 2 TB database, brought down to 1.2 TB with archiving.
ai: Estimating remediation effort from similar projects
r: Report skimmed: surprises during the conversion
Each item has an owner and a decision
Incompatible third-party add-on discovered late
Check each add-on with its vendor from Prepare

s4.obj: Set how the conversion will be done and within what limits.
act: Choosing the technical method: conversion with the SUM tool, one-step database migration (DMO)
Strategy for custom code: delete, fix, replace
s4.ex: Method: conversion and database migration in a single step. Downtime target: 48 hours, over a long weekend. Unused custom code will be deleted, not fixed.
r: Downtime target set without measurement: unachievable
Confirm it after the first mock conversion
Unused code fixed 'to be safe': wasted effort
Delete what has not run in two years, after validation

q1.obj: Authorize Explore: the impacts of the conversion are known.
act: Review of the Readiness Check and the conversion plan
q1.ex: Go-ahead granted with one condition: archiving must start immediately, as it determines the downtime duration.
ai: Consolidating the status of the criteria
r: Gate passed without an archiving plan: downtime too long later
Archiving written in as a condition tracked in committee

s5.s: Simplification items and new features to activate
s5.obj: Decide, for each change imposed by S/4HANA, how it will be absorbed, and which new features to activate.
act: Workshops by domain on the simplification items
Choosing the new features to activate: Fiori apps, new functions
Decision on retired functions, for example LE-WM
pre: Key users and process owners available
s5.ex: 45 items analyzed. Business Partner and the Universal Journal are mandatory. LE-WM is no longer the target: its replacement by EWM is planned in a second project. 12 Fiori apps selected to replace transactions.
ai: Explaining the items to the business
Matching the items against actual transaction usage
r: New features added en masse: the project becomes a hidden greenfield
Limit the conversion to what is mandatory, the rest after go-live
Mandatory item underestimated, like Business Partner
Treat the item as a separate workstream, with its own owner

s6.obj: Prepare the data in ECC so that the conversion goes through without blockers.
act: Converting customers and suppliers into Business Partners (CVI)
pre: Archiving rules validated by the business and legal
s6.ex: 45,000 customers and suppliers to convert: 3,200 in error at the first synchronization, because of incomplete addresses and duplicates. The finance checks reveal old gaps between general and cost accounting, fixed before the conversion.
r: Business Partner handled too late: conversion blocked
Start it in Explore, it is often the critical path
Finance gaps discovered during the conversion
Consistency checks launched early and repeated

s7.obj: Know precisely which custom code to keep, fix or delete.
act: Automatic checks (ATC) with the S/4HANA rules
Classification: delete, fix, replace with standard
pre: Usage statistics over at least a year
liv: Validated list of code to delete
s7.ex: Of 1,500 objects, 600 unused are deleted. The remaining 900 yield 2,300 findings, 70% of them automatically fixable.
ai: Spotting code that can be replaced by the standard
r: Usage measured over too short a period: a yearly program deleted by mistake
Statistics over at least twelve months, business validation
Remediation underestimated: Realize overloaded
Estimate from the ATC results, not from an overall guess

q2.obj: Authorize Realize: changes decided, remediation estimated, data in preparation.
act: Review of the remediation plan and Business Partner progress
q2.ex: Remediation plan estimated, Business Partner conversion under way with 3% errors remaining. Go-ahead granted.
r: Data still not prepared: mock conversions fail
Business Partner error threshold as a gate criterion

s8.s: Learn on a copy of production
s8.obj: Run a first technical conversion on a copy of production, in order to learn.
s8.ex: First conversion: 96 hours, double the target, and 37 blocking errors. This is normal: the first conversion is there to learn.
ai: Analyzing the conversion logs and grouping the errors
r: First conversion too late: no time left to learn
Run it at the start of Realize
Copy too old or incomplete: misleading results
Recent, complete copy of production

s9.s: Fix the code, adapt the processes
s9.obj: Fix the code and make the decided functional adaptations.
act: Adapting finance to the Universal Journal
s9.ex: The 900 objects are fixed in three months. The chart of accounts and cost accounting are adapted to the Universal Journal. The 12 Fiori apps are configured.
r: Double maintenance: ECC keeps evolving during the project
Freeze changes on ECC, or an organized retrofit process
Authorizations forgotten: users blocked at acceptance
Roles adapted from Realize

s10.s: Shorten and make the downtime reliable
s10.obj: Make the conversion reliable and bring it within the cutover window.
act: Conversions of the development and quality systems
Repeated mock conversions on production copies
pre: Errors from the first conversion fixed
s10.ex: Conversion 2: 70 hours. Conversion 3: 52 hours, thanks to archiving and parallelism. Conversion 4, in production conditions: 46 hours, within the 48-hour target.
ai: Analyzing durations by step to spot bottlenecks
r: Duration never reaches the target: the date slips
Alert threshold at each conversion, options prepared (more hardware, longer downtime)

s11.s: Everything works as before, and so do the changes
s11.obj: Prove that everything works as before, and that the changes work.
s11.ex: 2,000 regression tests, 60% of them automated. Defects come mostly from custom code and financial reports. Acceptance focuses on Business Partner, Fiori and the closing.
r: Insufficient regression: 'nothing has changed' is never true
Cover all critical processes, automate
Performance not tested: slow programs in production
Performance tests on heavy processing

s12.obj: Train users only on what changes.
act: List of visible changes by role
s12.ex: No new process: two hours of training for 900 users on Business Partner and Fiori apps, one day for the 60 accountants on the Universal Journal.
ai: Materials and short videos generated by role
r: Training judged unnecessary 'because it is the same system': confusion at go-live
Train at least on the visible changes

q3.obj: Authorize the final preparation: the conversion is under control and tested.
act: Review of the last mock conversion
pre: Last conversion within the duration target
q3.ex: Last conversion in 46 hours, zero blocking defects. Go-ahead granted.
r: Go-ahead with a conversion over time: downtime exceeded on D-day
Duration within the target as a blocking criterion

s13.obj: Prepare the production conversion minute by minute.
act: Runbook: transport freeze, interface shutdown, backup, conversion, checks
pre: Downtime window validated by the business
s13.ex: Runbook of 420 tasks, mostly technical. Point of no return: Saturday 8 pm. Fallback: restoring the ECC backup.
r: Fallback never tested: unusable
Restore tested during the rehearsal
Partners not told about the interface shutdown
Communication plan inside the runbook

s14.obj: Decide, on written criteria, whether to convert production.
s14.ex: 18 criteria green, 1 amber: a financial report still being corrected, with a manual workaround. Go.
r: Go despite a conversion over time
Duration criterion non-negotiable

s15.obj: Convert production and reopen the system.
act: Shutting down ECC and the interfaces
pre: Teams in place, SAP support notified
s15.ex: ECC shut down Thursday at 8 pm. Conversion in 44 hours. Accounting balances and stock identical before and after. Opening Monday at 6 am.
r: Reconciliation rushed: gaps discovered at closing
Before / after checks mandatory and signed
Fallback decision too late
Point of no return set and respected

s16.ex: Six weeks of hypercare. Incidents mostly concern the performance of a few custom programs and Fiori authorizations. First closing completed on time.
r: Slow programs not anticipated: business blocked
Performance monitoring from day one

act: Review of the handover to run
q4.ex: Exit declared six weeks after go-live.
r: Closure with open incidents
Formal takeover by run

s17.obj: Take advantage of S/4HANA: the conversion is only a starting point.
act: New Fiori apps and embedded analytics
Gradually reducing custom code towards Clean Core
s17.ex: Ternova launches the move to EWM, the adoption of new Fiori apps and the gradual cleanup of custom code.
r: Nothing after the conversion: paid for S/4HANA to keep running ECC
Roadmap and budget decided before go-live

transverse.obj: Run the conversion project: keep the technical side under control without losing the business.
act: Design authority: arbitration of code and changes
Freeze or control of changes on ECC
pre: Roles and bodies defined from Prepare
transverse.ex: Monthly committee, then weekly for the last two months. The main risk tracked throughout: the downtime duration.
ai: Caution: client data only in a tool approved by the client
r: Continuous changes on ECC during the project: unmanageable double maintenance
Change freeze or retrofit process
Watermelon effect on remediation progress
Factual indicators: objects fixed, errors remaining
